content.text: The gas limit in CCIP (Chainlink Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol) represents the maximum amount of gas that can be consumed to execute the `ccipReceive` function on the CCIP Receiver. It impacts the transaction fees for sending a CCIP message. Properly estimating the gas limit is crucial, as setting it too low can cause the transaction to revert, while setting it too high can lead to unnecessarily high fees. Unused gas is not reimbursed, so accuracy is important in determining the gas limit.
